title: Flood of errors when viewport size changes while using Texture2DRD
body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 4.5 stable or 4.6 dev 6

### System information

Windows 11 - Godot v4.6.dev6 - Vulkan (Forward+)

### Issue description

I'm using a couple of texture2DRDs to pass textures from a compute shader pipeline to a shader material. When the viewport size changes, I get a flood of errors, and the material fails to render for the first frame at the new size. This happens regardless of whether the textures themselves have changed size.

More detail: The material in question is an ocean shader, which uses two textures from a compute pipeline. One is a copy of the previous screen texture after a custom volumetric cloud pass, and the other is a 1024x1024 tiling heightmap generated via a series of compute shader passes. The screen (history) texture may change size, but the heightmap does not, yet the error appears when either one of these textures are used in the ocean shader.


In my compute code, I use:
 ```
var water = preload("res://.../water.tres")
var HistoryTexture2DRD : Texture2DRD = Texture2DRD.new()
...
#get history sampler from water shader
HistoryTexture2DRD = water.get_shader_parameter("HISTORY_TEXTURE") 

#without this line, we get an attempt to free an invalid RID on screen resizing
HistoryTexture2DRD.texture_rd_rid = RID()

#update the history sampler texture RID to the new (resized) history texture
HistoryTexture2DRD.texture_rd_rid = history_texture

#reset the history sampler in the water shader
water.set_shader_parameter("HISTORY_TEXTURE", HistoryTexture2DRD)
 ```

And in the water shader:
 ```
uniform sampler2D HISTORY_TEXTURE : repeat_disable, filter_linear_mipmap;
...
EMISSION= texture(HISTORY_TEXTURE, reflectedUV).rgb;
 ```

### Steps to reproduce

In a standard post-process compute pipeline, create a new `Texture2DRD`, set the `texture_rd_rid` property to the RID of a texture created in the compute pipeline, then use
`[customShaderMaterial].set_shader_parameter("texture_name", customTexture2DRD)`
and resize the viewport. This should result in the errors shown above for every frame that the screen is resized.
